text: Amazon CloudWatch is AWS's monitoring service, and it's already been watching every EC2 instance, S3 bucket, and VPC resource built so far in this course, with nothing to turn on. CloudWatch is really an umbrella over several pieces — metrics, alarms, logs, dashboards — much like Azure Monitor sits under every Azure resource in the Azure course. This chapter works through those pieces one at a time, starting with the simplest and most immediate: metrics.

The moment you launch an EC2 instance, it starts reporting metrics in the AWS/EC2 namespace automatically: CPUUtilization, NetworkIn and NetworkOut, DiskReadBytes and DiskWriteBytes, and StatusCheckFailed. These come from the hypervisor watching from outside the instance, which is exactly why they're free and automatic — and why they stop short of anything happening inside the guest operating system, like memory usage or free disk space, which take a dedicated agent to see.

By default, those metrics update every five minutes — basic monitoring, included at no extra charge. Turning on detailed monitoring, a checkbox at launch or an aws ec2 monitor-instances call afterward, raises that to one-minute intervals for a small per-instance cost. The underlying data is identical either way; detailed monitoring just catches a short CPU spike that a five-minute window might smooth right over.

AWS doesn't know about application-specific numbers like orders processed per minute, so you publish those yourself with the PutMetricData API, giving the value your own namespace and metric name. From that point on, it's stored and graphed exactly like a platform metric — including right next to CPUUtilization on a CloudWatch Dashboard, a customizable page of widgets you build to put related metrics side by side.

That's metrics and dashboards: automatic platform data plus anything custom you choose to publish, all visualized in one place without anyone having to watch it by hand. Next, Lesson 22 turns a metric threshold into something that actually taps someone on the shoulder — a CloudWatch Alarm that fires a real notification the moment a number crosses a line.
